concrete_capability_transition: CLI command skeleton with RuntimeUnavailable stub -> brownie status performs one bounded fail-closed stdio JSON-RPC runtime.status invocation against the existing Rust runtime

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Gives the official CLI a real runtime transport prerequisite for later brownie run objective execution while leaving execution decisions in Rust.
Provides the fixed runtime.status call path that later status and progress surfaces can reuse without raw RPC choreography.
Keeps permission, replay, recovery, Mode Pack, Product DoD, workspace mutation, and agent-loop policy out of the CLI while proving transport failure boundaries.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with progress_visualization and runtime_permission_enforcement support by connecting the CLI to the Rust runtime through one fixed status request.
answers.new_capability: brownie status becomes executable against the existing brownie-runtime host and returns bounded status or deterministic fail-closed errors.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: CLI-1 always returned RuntimeUnavailable; the VSIX transport does not give terminal users or headless callers a Rust CLI runtime boundary.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: CLI-2 would remain open and later run, resume, inspect, progress, and golden-journey work would lack a safe transport foundation.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from CLI-1 parser/binary work and from CLI-3 inspection UX because this closes only the minimal runtime connection and authority boundary.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The implementation uses the existing runtime.status method and adds no runtime JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No report, readiness, diagnostics wrapper, history, digest, verdict, inspection, preview, or summary surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime semantics are unchanged; user-visible CLI behavior changes from a stubbed runtime_unavailable status to a real bounded runtime.status invocation.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The CLI gains the fixed transport path needed before it can expose runtime-owned autonomous objective execution safely.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes CLI Product DoD gap CLI-2 only and leaves CLI-3 through CLI-10 open for bounded follow-up phases.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: The current and CLI-2 phase-value manifests change because CLI-2 is the active phase. Review confirms guard semantics are not weakened and the phase is not wrapper-only.

exit_criteria: brownie status invokes a runtime process and succeeds on a valid runtime.status JSON-RPC response
the runtime request method is fixed to runtime.status and cannot be caller-selected
JSON-RPC version, response id, result/error exclusivity, and bounded RuntimeStatus shape are validated
malformed JSON, JSON-RPC error, mismatched id, runtime exit, missing binary, and timeout failures are deterministic and fail closed
--json status emits bounded machine-readable status or error payloads
brownie run does not start an agent loop in CLI-2
develop remains absent as a primary command
no runtime JSON-RPC method is added for this phase
behavior_evidence: brownie-cli integration tests execute brownie status against fake runtime processes and assert request method, success output, JSON output, malformed JSON, JSON-RPC error, mismatched id, missing binary, and timeout behavior.
brownie-cli integration tests execute brownie status against the real brownie-runtime binary when built in the workspace.
brownie-cli unit tests validate response-id checking and bounded RuntimeStatus parsing.
Existing CLI tests continue proving help/version/invalid invocation and develop rejection.

accepted_capability: brownie status now uses a thin fail-closed stdio JSON-RPC transport to call the existing Rust runtime.status method.
The CLI validates JSON-RPC response shape and id before printing bounded status or deterministic errors.
behavior_evidence: Integration tests use fake runtime processes to verify the exact runtime.status request and fail-closed response validation behavior.
An integration test invokes the real brownie-runtime binary for brownie status when the workspace binary is available.
cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace, cargo test --workspace, diagnostics guard, phase-value guard, product-completion guard, and VSIX checks remain required validation.
safety_boundary: CLI-2 adds no runtime JSON-RPC method and exposes no arbitrary JSON-RPC passthrough.
CLI-2 does not implement brownie run execution or a second CLI-owned agent loop.
CLI-2 does not duplicate permission, replay, recovery, Mode Pack, Product DoD, product-completion, workspace mutation, ledger, or agent-loop policy in the CLI.
CLI-2 does not expose raw prompts, provider responses, file contents, stdout/stderr payloads, commands, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, or secrets.
non_goals: No resume, inspect, list, or mode-list runtime behavior beyond preserving fail-closed unsupported responses.
No daemon lifecycle manager, TUI, REPL, shell integration, plugin system, or packaging release.
No workspace mutation, provider execution, controlled tool execution, verifier execution, network access, git execution, or service control.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected arbitrary JSON-RPC passthrough because the CLI must be a human workflow surface, not an RPC mirror.
Rejected adding a new runtime RPC because existing runtime.status is sufficient for this slice.
Rejected implementing brownie run in this phase because that would mix CLI-4 autonomous objective execution into CLI-2.
Rejected CLI-owned workflow, permission, replay, recovery, Mode Pack, Product DoD, and workspace mutation policy because Rust runtime authority remains the architecture invariant.
technical_debt: CLI-3 through CLI-10 remain open Product DoD gaps after CLI-2.
Runtime binary discovery and packaging can be hardened in CLI-8 without changing CLI-2 transport authority semantics.
next_capability_rationale: After CLI-2 lands, CLI-3 should expand read-only status and inspection UX through existing runtime methods using the same thin transport boundary.
Product completion is denied until all required CLI Product DoD gaps, blocking debt, and required_before_release debt are closed.
